learn.title: Point-slope form
learn.body: If you know the slope $m$ and one point $(x_1,y_1)$, write $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$. It is a fast way to build an equation without finding $b$ first.

learn.title: Slope 2 through $(3,1)$
learn.body: Put the numbers in, then tidy up.

learn.title: Line through $(1,2)$ and $(3,8)$
learn.body: Two points first give the slope.

learn.title: Standard form
learn.body: Standard form is $Ax+By=C$. For $y=2x-5$ move the $x$ term: $2x-y=5$. It is handy for intercepts.
In $2x+3y=12$ set $y=0$ for the $x$-intercept (6) and $x=0$ for the $y$-intercept (4).

questions.prompt: A line has slope 4 and passes through $(2,5)$. Which is its point-slope equation?

questions.explanation: It is the same slope as in slope-intercept form.

questions.prompt: A line has slope 2 and passes through $(3,1)$. What is its $y$-intercept?
A line passes through $(1,2)$ and $(3,8)$. What is $y$ when $x=0$?

questions.explanation: Subtract $y$ and add 5 to both sides: $2x-y=5$.

questions.prompt: Find the line through $(1,2)$ and $(3,8)$. Put the steps in order.
questions.explanation: Slope first, then one point in point-slope form, then tidy up.
